maria-ops: FYI - after the stream-batcher v3 roll we see a ~18% P95 latency bump on chat-workload and KV/prefix cache hit-rate dropped ~22%. Posting quick profiler snippets and a couple of experiments we tried.

infra-bot: deploy-log: canary @ 1954320950 -> stream-batcher:v3, rollout -> full @ 1954320980. No other infra changes in that window. :robot_face:

maria-ops: PROFILE summary:
```
KV_CACHE_HIT_RATE: 0.58 -> 0.36
P95_latency(ms): 138 -> 163
CPU_cycles/token: +8%
flame: /traces/1954321000/flame.svg
```

oliver: Do we know what changed in v3 internals? I vaguely recall v3 enabled stream mixing + dynamic kernel choice for mixed sequence batches. If kernel selection started preferring a different matmul path for long sequences, that could interact poorly when KV cache hits fall. Can you paste the trace id?

maria-ops: trace id attached above (flame.svg). Also noticed batch composition skew: more small-prefix requests ended up mixed with long-context ones in same batch. Suspect keying and cohorting got more churn.

raj: Two quick theories: (1) batch mixing reduced effective KV reuse because cache keys were built from padded token arrays (we key on full tensor instead of trimmed prefix), (2) cohort window enlarged so affinity diluted. Quick experiment suggestion: flip `batch_cohort_window_ms` from 200 -> 50 and enable `kv_key_trim_pads=true`. Minimal surface: restart batcher workers.

sophie: I added a low-overhead probe to emit anonymized kv-key hash + cohort id for a sample of requests. Query to inspect: 
```
-- in analytics cluster
SELECT cohort, count(*) as calls, avg(is_kv_hit::int) as hit_rate
FROM kv_probe_logs
WHERE ts > now() - interval '30 minutes'
GROUP BY cohort
ORDER BY hit_rate ASC
LIMIT 10;
```
Results show two cohorts with hit_rate ~0.18 and a few with >0.7. That suggests mixing across cohorts.

leo: Repro steps I ran locally: 
```
./bin/loadtest --rps 250 --model redwood-v1 --batch-mode stream --cohort-window-ms 200 --run-id repro-1954
# results
kv_hit_rate: 0.61
p95: 142ms

# then
./bin/loadtest --rps 250 --model redwood-v1 --batch-mode stream --cohort-window-ms 50 --kv-key-trim-pads true
kv_hit_rate: 0.78
p95: 126ms
```
So shrinking the cohort window + trimming pads seems promising.

oliver: Interesting. Might also be interaction with kernel selection heuristics: when batching mixes seq-len extremes, the scheduler chooses a conservative kernel with worse throughput per token. If that kernel path assumes cheaper KV lookups (higher hit-rate) it could lead to compounding regression when hits fall. We should capture `kernel_id` per request in the probe.

maria-ops: Agreed. Action items: (1) Sophie + Raj to add kernel_id to kv_probe_logs and flip `kv_key_trim_pads` behind a feature flag for canary. (2) Leo to run A/B loadtest with cohort-window 50 vs 200. (3) If no improvement in 1h, roll back stream-batcher v3 to v2. I'll schedule a 20m sync at 11:30 to review. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

raj: I'll own the feature flag + quick rollback plan. Patch I'll land: `batcher/flags.go` add `KVKeyTrimPads` and `CohortWindowMs`. Minimal change and feature-flagged.

sophie: I'll instrument kernel_id + kv_key_hash sample (first 64 bits) and push the probe pipeline to staging. Will also add a dashboard showing per-cohort hit-rate and average kernel cycles/token.

maria-ops: Thanks all. If someone sees the P95 keep climbing, add `status:urg` in the channel so we escalate.

oliver: One more note: captured a perf diff that shows CPU cycles/token up ~8% when global kv_hit_rate < 0.4, consistent with the observed numbers. Dump attached in the trace.

sophie: I'll follow up with a short write-up and the SQL saved query after I push the probe. Taking ownership. :white_check_mark:

leo: I'll run the A/B tests now and report results in this thread in ~30m.
